title: ZEKIROV v. "THE FORMER YUGOSLAV REPUBLIC OF MACEDONIA"
summary: In the case of Zekirov v. "the former Yugoslav Republic of Macedonia," the applicant, Mr. Zekirov, identified as a member of the Roma community, brought a complaint against the Macedonian authorities. The case highlighted the vulnerability of Roma individuals facing discrimination and restrictions on their freedom of movement, a recurring issue for Roma and Travellers across Europe. Mr. Zekirov alleged that he had suffered discriminatory treatment and violations of his rights under the European Convention on Human Rights, specifically concerning freedom of movement and protection from discrimination. The events giving rise to the case occurred in Macedonia, where Mr. Zekirov claimed that state actions had unjustly limited his ability to travel and had treated him differently due to his Roma identity. Before the European Court of Human Rights could issue a substantive judgment, the parties reached a friendly settlement: the government agreed to pay Mr. Zekirov 2,500 euros to cover non-pecuniary damages and costs, resolving the matter. The Court, satisfied that the settlement respected human rights, struck the case from its list. This outcome is significant as it demonstrates the potential for redress through the Convention system for Roma and Travellers, who have historically faced systemic barriers to equal treatment and freedom of movement in Europe.
